articles.title: Seahawks Coach Mike Macdonald Provides Sam Darnold Injury Update
articles.summary: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald expects Sam Darnold to return to practice this week, but the quarterback’s status for Week 3 is uncertain.
articles.body: Seattle Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald expects Sam Darnold to return to practice this week, but the quarterback's status for this weekend's game against the Washington Commanders remains uncertain. Darnold sustained a glute injury in the first series of Seattle's season opener against the New England Patriots. Drew Lock took over and helped the Seahawks to a 13-10 victory, then started Sunday's 31-7 victory over the Arizona Cardinals. There was no timeline announced for Darnold's return, but it appeared he could be back soon. "Right now, the plan is for him to be out there in some capacity, and we’ll go from there," Macdonald said Monday. "How much? We’ll see from here to Wednesday what that number is, but right now that’s the goal." Lock completed 19 of 26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns — all to star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba — against the Cardinals. As of Monday, the Seahawks hadn't determined how much work Darnold would get in practice ahead of the game at Washington. "Obviously, this week is a little bit different with Sam’s situation being a little more up in the air going throughout the week," Macdonald said. "So this is a little different approach in terms of our process about how we’ll handle our preparation throughout the week." In the opener, Lock went 16 of 22 for 187 yards and a touchdown, also to Smith-Njigba. Lock has not committed a turnover. Macdonald said the transition to Lock has been smooth. The 29-year-old has mostly served as a backup since 2021 and saw little action last season as Darnold led Seattle to the Super Bowl title. "I didn’t sense much difference in the attitude or the emotion of the team last week, which is a tremendous compliment to Drew. The things he’s been able to do, day-in and day-out, the types of practices and type of football he’s played out on the practice field throughout training camp, throughout his opportunities in the preseason, I sense a lot of confidence in what he brings to the table," Macdonald said. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Could Morgan Rielly’s new role under Jim Hiller reshape the Maple Leafs’ NHL defense this new season
articles.summary: NHL News: Discover how new Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller plans to revitalize Morgan Rielly's role in the 2026-27 NHL season, focusing on offensive opportunities and strategic pairings.
articles.body: Morgan Rielly’s play of late with former Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Craig Berube has been under fire, especially with respect to his overall play defensively and consistency. More talk about his future with the organization was generated in the offseason because of that.Rielly was a major topic of criticism during the offseason, with some parts of the Toronto fanbase and media calling for the Maple Leafs to consider trading him. But Hiller’s comments suggest the new head coach is more focused on capitalising on Rielly’s strengths rather than revisiting those concerns.What did Jim Hiller say about Morgan Rielly’s role?Jim Hiller stated Morgan Rielly is getting a fresh start and that the Toronto Maple Leafs are expecting a strong season from their veteran defenseman.The 32-year-old defenceman is staying with Toronto as training camp begins. His role, experience, and offensive ability still make him an important part of the Maple Leafs’ blue line.Morgan Rielly might get more chances in offensive situations this upcoming NHL season, Jim Hiller has indicated.Hiller also mentioned Radko Gudas as a potential defensive partner for Rielly. The tandem would combine Rielly’s puck-moving and offensive skills with Gudas’ physicality and defensive experience for Toronto.The coaching staff is also expected to give Rielly some looks with some of Toronto’s top-six forwards. That could give the defenseman more to do on offensive-zone shifts and allow him to have a more direct impact on the Maple Leafs’ attack.What does this mean for Toronto Maple Leafs?The comments offered an early glimpse into how Jim Hiller intends to handle Morgan Rielly now that he’s taken over as Toronto’s head coach.Rather than constrict Rielly's role after a rough stretch, Hiller appears prepared to give him a crucial role. The method stresses the need to create opportunities for Rielly’s skating, puck movement, and offensive instincts to be put to use.When the 2026-27 NHL season begins, the Toronto Maple Leafs will be watching Rielly’s play very closely. Alongside Radko Gudas and other more high-profile forwards, his deployment may be a key sub-plot in the early part of the campaign.Hiller said he understood the criticism directed at Rielly, but he did not agree. He said he has confidence in the defenseman and expects Rielly to have a good year.The message is a definite change of emphasis under the new coaching staff. Rielly enters training camp with an opportunity to reassert himself as a key cog in the Toronto Maple Leafs’ defensive and offensive transition game.Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller will give Morgan Rielly a clean slate to start the 2026-27 NHL season. articles.title: Connor McDavid’s $4 million Edmonton mansion: Inside the NHL star’s luxury home, custom design, sports court, entertainment spaces and lifestyle
articles.summary: NHL News: Connor McDavid’s success with the Edmonton Oilers hasn’t just been on the ice; it’s allowed the NHL superstar to create a highly customized home in Ed.
articles.body: Connor McDavid’s success with the Edmonton Oilers hasn’t just been on the ice; it’s allowed the NHL superstar to create a highly customized home in Edmonton. The mansion, which is purported to be valued at approximately $4 million, was constructed to suit his routines on and off the ice.The three-story property near Edmonton’s North Saskatchewan River valley was developed with interior designer Lauren Kyle. The 8,000-square-foot home features large windows, modern furnishings and a minimalist color palette of black, white and earth tones.Connor McDavid’s $4 million mansion reveals luxury lifestyleHaving been unable to find an Edmonton property that fit their vision, McDavid and Kyle are said to have decided to create a home of their own. The result is a large three-storey house with well-thought-out living, entertainment and training areas.The main level has a chef’s kitchen with a huge marble island and a dining area with a secret bar behind sliding brass doors. The living area is also kept on the slimline theme, with TVs concealed behind custom metal panels.Mansion featureDetailsLocationEdmonton, AlbertaApprox. size8,000 square feetFloorsThreeReported valueAround $4 millionDesignModern minimalistSports facilityIndoor half-basketball courtConnor McDavid’s mansion showcases Edmonton luxuryThe basement has an indoor half-basketball court that gives McDavid room to rollerblade, handle pucks and train during Edmonton’s harsh winter months. He uses a home gym to stay in shape for the physical demands of the NHL.There’s also a private movie theater, wine display and a moody speakeasy-style bar, all on the same level. These additions serve the basement not only with a functional training purpose but also with an entertainment-oriented atmosphere.Upstairs is more private, with a primary suite that features a hotel-style bed and pop-up TV. An open closet is said to be inspired by Yves Saint Laurent, and a two-person infrared sauna offers yet another wellness touch.Connor McDavid built around hockey and hostingThe open-plan layout was also designed for entertaining. Reports say the home is appropriate for hosting teammates and their families, and that McDavid, the captain of the Edmonton Oilers, has used the home in that capacity.The kitchen, dining and living areas of the property flow through to create a large social setting. Floor-to-ceiling windows bring natural light into the residence and frame views to Edmonton’s surrounding river valley landscape.The mansion combines high-end design with elements directly related to McDavid’s career. Training and recovery can be part of everyday life with the indoor court, gym and sauna, without leaving the property.The special touches add a more relaxed character to the home. Lenard, Kyle’s Bernedoodle, is said to make appearances in some of the home’s decorative touches.So, the Edmonton mansion is more than just a luxury property. McDavid’s home features custom sports amenities, entertainment spaces and a winter-friendly design that reflects how it was built around the demands of an NHL career without losing a contemporary, private family environment.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shane McMahon vs Stephanie McMahon net worth comparison: Which WWE executive sibling has more wealth in 2026
articles.summary: WWE News: Stephanie McMahon and Shane McMahon grew up as two of the most recognisable members of the McMahon family. Both followed their father Vince McMahon in.
articles.body: Stephanie McMahon and Shane McMahon grew up as two of the most recognisable members of the McMahon family. Both followed their father Vince McMahon into WWE, but their careers eventually took different paths. Stephanie became a senior WWE executive and one of the company’s biggest on-screen personalities.Shane also worked in WWE management before leaving the company and exploring business opportunities outside wrestling. He later returned to WWE as a part-time performer and became known for his high-risk matches. Both siblings have built careers in business and entertainment, but their financial paths have been very different.Stephanie McMahon vs Shane McMahon net worth in 2026Based on the estimates by celebrity net worth, Stephanie McMahon has a net worth of around $400 million with her husband Paul “Triple H” Levesque, while Shane McMahon has an estimated net worth of around $200 million.CategoryStephanie McMahonShane McMahonEstimated 2026 net worth$400 million combined with Triple H$200 millionMain WWE roleExecutive, performer and former Co-CEOExecutive and part-time performerMajor WWE positionChief Brand Officer, Chairwoman and Co-CEOExecutive VP of Global MediaWWE/TKO wealthMajor historical WWE stakeHistorical WWE stake, later less clearly documentedOutside businessMedia, branding and entertainmentTechnology, media and investmentCurrent WWE roleMedia personality and brand ambassadorOccasional wrestling appearancesSpousePaul “Triple H” LevesqueMarissa MazzolaMajor media workStephanie’s Places, What’s Your Story?Television and wrestling projectsStephanie’s wealth has been closely connected to WWE equity. A March 2023 WWE filing showed that she beneficially owned 1,940,190 WWE shares. When WWE and UFC were combined under TKO Group Holdings later that year, WWE shares were converted into TKO Class A shares.At a TKO share price of $190, that historical position would have been worth roughly $369 million. However, later changes to her holdings are not as clearly disclosed, so this should not be treated as a current exact valuation.Stephanie also held several major executive positions during her WWE career. She served as Chief Brand Officer before becoming Chairwoman and Co-CEO. In 2022, her total WWE compensation was reported at about $14.28 million, including salary, stock awards and other compensation.Shane’s financial story is different. He worked his way through WWE’s business operations before becoming Executive Vice President of Global Media. He left WWE in 2009 and moved into technology and media investments.One of his most notable business ventures was YOU On Demand, a Chinese video-on-demand company. He later became involved with Ideanomics, which focused on electric vehicles and related technology.Shane also maintained a connection with WWE as a performer. Company filings show that he received about $1.31 million in 2021 and approximately $828,000 in 2022 for his WWE performer work.The siblings also had different relationships with WWE ownership. Shane’s historical WWE holdings were substantial, but later public filings made his position harder to track. A 2013 filing showed that he beneficially owned 1,541,204 WWE shares.Stephanie, meanwhile, became one of the company’s most visible executives before stepping away from day-to-day leadership in 2023.Outside WWE, Stephanie has continued building her media profile. She launched Stephanie’s Places with ESPN and Omaha Productions and later hosted the interview podcast What’s Your Story?. She was also inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2026.Shane’s post-WWE business ventures have been more varied. His involvement with Ideanomics ultimately faced significant financial problems, with the company filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in 2024.The siblings therefore have very different career stories. articles.title: U.S. Weekend Stock Watch: Cavan Sullivan Stays Hot; Tim Weah On The Way Out?
articles.summary: Alexi Lalas takes a look at the U.S. player pool in his Weekend Stock Watch.
articles.body: A new era of the United States men's national team is upon us. Yes, Mauricio Pochettino is still the head coach, and many of the familiar faces from the 2026 FIFA World Cup will be in the mix for 2030, but the competition is as stiff as ever, and at positions that were previously viewed as untouchable. Let's take a look at where some of the key figures in the U.S. player pool stand ahead of the international window in Alexi Lalas' U.S. Weekend Stock Watch: Stock Up: Christian Pulisic ⬆️ Alexi: You've got to be a little happy — and dare I say, proud — of seeing Christian Pulisic, given what's happened over this past year and even what's happened recently, starting and not just making an impact, but being voted the best player, being involved in both goals and being associated with a moment of positivity that Christian Pulisic and AC Milan needed. Stock Up: Cavan Sullivan ⬆️ Alexi: You can make a case that, in this window, even if Christian Pulisic had been involved, there are more poeple excited about seeing Cavan Sullivan than Christian Pulisic. We know who Christian Pulisic is. That doesn't mean he can't improve, but he is what he is. America is looking for young talent and new look when it comes to the national team and that's why there's so much tension with Cavan Sullivan as he comes into this new camp, and he comes in on fire. Stock Up: USA In The EFL ⬆️ Alexi: We all recognize that many of these players are looking for a foot in the door when it comes to Europe, and in that sense, they're not just getting there; they're now actually playing and playing well and scoring goals. It's fun to see this brigade of young players who are using the Championship for what it is and what it isn't as this stepping stone. Stock Up: Johnny Cardoso ⬆️ Alexi: This is great, to be associated with the type of win, but I feel like a broken record with Johnny. This is what he is and what he has done. He gets our hopes up, but ultimately, can he translate it if and when he is with the U.S. men's national team? You can be a really, really good player, and sometimes it just doesn't translate, and you can bang your head as to why it doesn't. You just have to guard against this idea that you're leaving talent on the sideline; that we are wasting talent. Stock Down: Ricardo Pepi ⬇️ Alexi: If you're looking at it for the Pepi fanbase, this sucks because, finally, he gets this opportunity after being second fiddle to Balogun, and fairly so, to come in and claim it for himself, especially in this new-look national team. On the other side, it's just another opportunity because I think it's going to be wide-open up top in this camp when it comes to who plays. Stock Down: Tim Weah ⬇️ Alexi: If you're Pochettino, do you say ‘I can still get something out of him,’ even with all of these changes and his obvious inability to adjust under that? There was a time that he was in pen there on that right side, and I wasn't alone. Times have changed. Yunus Musah is back in the fold and Tim Weah looks to be on the way out. Stock Down: Americans At Celtic ⬇️ Alexi: I'm all for supporting your team, I'm all for die-hard fandom out there, but it has to come with some perspective. There's nothing romantic about this, there's nothing cool about this, and as far as that purity pest about how much you care about your team, it's not relevant to what you set on fire, including the bus.

articles.title: Reconocimiento facial en El Campín: cómo funciona el sistema FacePass para ingresar al estadio
articles.standfirst: Ingreso biométrico en El Campín: cómo registrarse en FacePass y a quiénes aplica la medida
articles.summary: Ingreso biométrico en El Campín: cómo registrarse en FacePass y a quiénes aplica la medida
articles.body: El Estadio Nemesio Camacho El Campín marca un hito en la modernización y seguridad de los espectáculos deportivos en Bogotá. Con el inicio del plan piloto del sistema FacePass, desarrollado por la tiquetera TuBoleta, la tribuna Oriental del escenario capitalino estrena la tecnología de reconocimiento facial para el ingreso de espectadores. La prueba de fuego se realiza durante el partido entre Independiente Santa Fe y Deportivo Cali, correspondiente a la jornada 12 de la Liga BetPlay. FacePass es una solución de biometría facial diseñada para transformar y agilizar la experiencia de los hinchas al momento de ingresar al estadio. La iniciativa nace como respuesta directa a los incidentes violentos registrados un mes atrás durante el encuentro entre Independiente Santa Fe y América de Cali, donde la invasión del terreno de juego por la disputa de un trapo impidió la individualización rápida de los infractores. Hasta ahora, el acceso al estadio se realizaba únicamente mediante la boleta digital descargada en la app de la tiquetera, lo que dificultaba a las autoridades la identificación de quienes cometían actos vandálicos. Según la información suministrada por TuBoleta y la directiva de Santa Fe, este primer periodo de pruebas permitirá: De ser exitosa la prueba, el sistema podría extenderse gradualmente a las demás localidades del escenario deportivo, posicionando a Bogotá a la vanguardia de la tecnología para la convivencia en el fútbol.

articles.title: Eagles Reportedly Sign Former Pro Bowl CB Kenny Moore II To Practice Squad
articles.summary: After being released by the Indianapolis Colts earlier this offseason, veteran cornerback Kenny Moore II has officially found a new home with the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body: After being released by the Indianapolis Colts earlier this offseason, veteran cornerback Kenny Moore II has officially found a new home with the Philadelphia Eagles. On Tuesday morning, Moore signed with the Philadelphia Eagles practice squad. According to NFL Network, he is expected to eventually earn a one-year deal worth up to $3 million while contributing at both nickel cornerback and safety. Moore, 31, was a Pro Bowler with the Colts in 2021 and brings valuable experience to the Eagles' secondary. With defensive coordinator Vic Fangio looking to maximize Moore's versatility across multiple positions, he has a real opportunity to make a big impact. The Eagles boast one of the most versatile secondaries, led by Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean. General manager Howie Roseman continues to show his knack for finding value, consistently buying low on talented players who have the potential to make an impact. After spending his entire nine-year career in Indianapolis, Moore leaves behind a strong final season with the Colts. He recorded 55 tackles, 1.5 sacks, six pass deflections, two forced fumbles and an interception while continuing to anchor their secondary. With his versatility, the Eagles could tap into the Pro Bowl form Moore showed earlier in his career. Fangio’s defense is young and undergoing plenty of change, making an experienced veteran of Moore's caliber a valuable addition to the room. Through two games, the Eagles are allowing 21 points per game, but the pass defense has looked solid overall. Even after facing manageable offenses in the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans, this group will soon be put to the test as the NFC schedule toughens up.

articles.title: Cameron Menzies upsets Gian van Veen to win second title of 2026
articles.summary: Scotland's Cameron Menzies celebrates his second tournament win of the year after beating Gian van Veen to the Players Championship 29 title in Den Bosch.
articles.body:
Scotland's Cameron Menzies is celebrating his second tournament win of the year after beating Gian van Veen to the Players Championship 29 title in Den Bosch.

Menzies raced into a 5-0 lead against the home favourite, who is third in the PDC rankings, before prevailing 8-4.

"To go and win another ProTour is awesome. I'm so happy," said Menzies.

"This is my fifth year on the tour and I've won four ProTours. That's not bad I suppose.

"My aim is to make a good life for myself. That's the aim that I think is achievable, but winning a major and having a good run at the World Championship would be amazing.

"I've put more effort in this year than I ever have because I nearly lost it all and I'm grateful to be in this position."

Menzies, ranked 26th, had considered quitting darts earlier this year after damaging his hand while angrily punching a drinks table following a first-round exit at the World Championship.

In July, the Scot was victorious at Players Championship 23 in Leicester.

Later that month, Menzies beat world number two Luke Humphries in the first round of the World Matchplay, only to fall ill in his next match.

En route to the final in Den Bosch, he got past Kevin Doets, Jeffrey de Graaf, Wessel Nijman, Benjamin Pratnemer, Jim Long and Nick Kenny.

articles.title: Chargers make ridiculously underwhelming tight end move after losing David Njoku to IR
articles.summary: The Chargers signed a practice squad tight end Tuesday. After losing tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar to injury, the Chargers added Hayden Rucci to t...
articles.body:
The Chargers signed a practice squad tight end Tuesday.

After losing tight ends David Njoku and Charlie Kolar to injury , the Chargers added Hayden Rucci to the active roster from Jacksonville 's practice squad.

Rucci won't be the primary tight end for the LA offense as the Chargers plan to utilize Oronde Gadsden II with Njoku and Kolar on injured reserve. The Chargers also have two tight ends on their practice squad, Evan Svoboda and Patrick Herbert (brother of quarterback Justin Herbert ), and could elevate them.

Rucci has played four games in the NFL, recording only a tackle on special teams. The tight end was an undrafted free agent in 2024 and signed with the Dolphins.

He was quite the journeyman last season as he spent time with the Lions toward the end of the campaign and joined the 49ers in the offseason. Now, Rucci will get an opportunity with the struggling Chargers.

LA's 0-2 start to the season has been the most disappointing beginning to a campaign in the Jim Harbaugh era. The Chargers opened the last two seasons 2-0.

Nothing has quite panned out for the team, including its free agent class as more than half of those players have been sidelined by injury (including Njoku and Kolar). Perhaps the most shocking discovery for the Chargers this year has been a lackluster offense despite new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

There are a lot of questions that need to be answered for LA, and Rucci's addition doesn't quite seem to be a needle-mover.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé recalls turning down Liverpool despite talks with Jürgen Klopp
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappé has discussed what led him to move to Paris Saint-Germain over Liverpool in 2017, despite his mom and agent both urging him to join Jürgen Klop...
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has revealed he contemplated joining Liverpool back in 2017, but dismissed his agent and mother's appeals to relocate to Anfield in favor of a transfer to Paris Saint-Germain .

The Real Madrid forward was merely 18 years old when he sat down with Jürgen Klopp and Liverpool executives aboard a private aircraft, with the group conducting discussions while flying over Nice in Southern France.

Mbappé was representing AS Monaco at the time and would eventually reject the Reds' overtures to sign for PSG - completing the move to Paris via an initial loan arrangement that featured a mandatory £165.7 million (around $214 million) purchase clause, as per the Liverpool Echo .

However, the striker's agent and mother, Fayza Lamari, had been eager for him to join Liverpool instead.

"It was while I was playing in Monaco," he recalled to The Athletic . "I had to take a decision. And yes, I was close to Liverpool. My mum was a big fan of Jürgen Klopp and the favorite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.

"I didn't listen because I wanted to play in my city, Paris. I didn't want to leave my country before I was someone. But yes, my mum was always saying, 'Liverpool - you're going to be there, playing at Anfield, it's going to be insane for you.' I was like, 'OK!'

"She went there (for) the first step of the negotiations. She went to the city, the stadium, she met the people. She was like, 'It's a wonderful club, everybody's so kind, it's a family club, a big club.'

"She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"All the time we were talking. 'What do you think, Mum?' She'd say, 'For me, you have to go to Liverpool. I said, 'OK, OK, OK!' because Jürgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him."

Mbappé acknowledges he was drawn to the prospect of joining Klopp's Liverpool. However, in the end, he couldn't turn down the appeal of his boyhood club, as he revealed his reasons for declining the Merseyside side.

"I remember we were on the plane and we were turning around and around in the air while he (Klopp) was explaining his project. I said, 'You don't need to convince me. You're Jürgen Klopp, it's Liverpool, a great club, so of course if I'm here, I have some interest.

"But I have other things, other projects, that are also good.' I said to him, 'Whatever decision I take is going to be a good decision because we are talking about some of the biggest clubs in the world.'

"It's a funny story. But in the end, I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my home town."

articles.title: Could Pellegrini or Patric Get Reinstated in Lazio Squad List?
articles.summary: When Lazio released their Serie A squad list at the start of the month, the big surprise was the omission of Luca Pellegrini and Patric.Why Lazio Excluded Lu...
articles.body:
When Lazio released their Serie A squad list at the start of the month, the big surprise was the omission of Luca Pellegrini and Patric .

Why Lazio Excluded Luca Pellegrini & Patric

While it was evident that the two defenders are at the bottom of Gennaro Gattuso's pecking order, observers thought they would still retain their places in the squad. Instead, the Biancocelesti preferred to leave two vacant slots, with Lazio sporting director Angelo Fabiani later explaining that the idea was to make room for potential late arrivals on free transfers.

The Italian capital club has since signed Diogo Leite , who filled one of the two available spots. The club was also contemplating a move for Mauro Icardi , but Gattuso insisted he's happy with his current options in attack. Therefore, one spot remains available, while two senior players remain on the outs.

According to Il Messaggero , there are no immediate plans to reinstate either Pellegrini or Patic in the coming weeks. That being said, the Spanish defender still has some hope of making his way back to the squad at some point. On the contrary, the Italian left-back is expected to remain out until January, when he'll be placed on the transfer market.

Why Patric is More Likely to Return Than Pellegrini

At the moment, Gattuso already has five full-backs vying for two roles in the shape of left-backs Nuno Tavares and Alfonso Pedraza , plus right-backs Adam Marusic, Romano Floriani Mussolini , and Manuel Lazzari . Therefore, Pellegrini is considered surplus to requirements.

(Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

On the other hand, Lazio currently have four centre-backs in the squad: Josip Sutalo, Oliver Provstgaard , Danilho Doekhi , and Leite. Hence, an experienced profile like Patric could serve as an additional option, not to mention his status as a locker-room senator.

articles.title: Jay McEvoy: Two countries embroiled in battle for Man United talent’s allegiance
articles.summary: 1Manchester United starlet Jay McEvoy has reportedly found himself caught between two countries fighting to secure his international future.Superb talentMcEv...
articles.body:
Manchester United starlet Jay McEvoy has reportedly found himself caught between two countries fighting to secure his international future.

McEvoy is widely regarded as one of the most promising talents within the club's current academy ranks.

The 2008-born midfielder has dazzled with his vision, silky ability on the ball and mature reading of the game. In addition, he possesses brilliant athleticism and a calmness under pressure that belies his years.

In 2024, Italian newspaper Tuttomercato likened McEvoy to Barcelona and Spain legend Xavi.

Tuttomercato wrote, "McEvoy displays excellent reading of game situations and possesses good athleticism, making him a complete and versatile player for Manchester United's midfield."

He scored last weekend as the Under-18s put Wolverhampton Wanderers to the sword in a thumping 6-0 victory.

McEvoy scored United's third goal of the match.

According to the Daily Mail , two European nations are fighting hard for McEvoy to commit his future to them.

The newspaper reveals that Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland are both determined to land McEvoy, who is facing a massive career decision.

He has represented both countries at youth level.

The Daily Mail report, "Both the Irish FA, which looks after Northern Ireland, and the Football Association of Ireland, which governs football in Republic of Ireland, have made pitches to McEvoy and his family."

"Confidential has been told Northern Ireland manager Michael O'Neill is aware of the situation and is set to sit down with the player and his family in the coming weeks in a decisive move to keep him out of the clutches of the FAI."

Meanwhile, Michael Carrick and his players return to action on 10 October when they host Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford.

articles.summary: Daizen Maeda received a rapturous reception from the Celtic support after making an emotional return to Parkhead on Sunday.Daizen Maeda says his Celtic goodb...
articles.body:
Daizen Maeda received a rapturous reception from the Celtic support after making an emotional return to Parkhead on Sunday.

Daizen Maeda says his Celtic goodbyes ahead of kickoff. Celtic v Rangers, Scottish Premiership. Sunday 20 September 2026. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

The former Hoops forward was back at Celtic Park just months after completing his move to Ipswich Town, with Sky Sports Scotland sharing footage of the Japan international inside the stadium ahead of the clash with Rangers.

Celtic confirmed on Saturday that Maeda had personally asked to return to Paradise so he could properly thank supporters for the backing shown to him and his family throughout his four-and-a-half years in Glasgow.

The 28-year-old never had the opportunity to say farewell at Celtic Park when his move to Ipswich was completed, but he finally got that chance on Sunday.

Maeda was introduced to the crowd before kick-off and was greeted with a huge ovation from the Celtic support as he made his way onto the pitch.

It was a fitting reception for a player who enjoyed a hugely successful spell in Glasgow.

Maeda departed Celtic having made 212 appearances for the club, scoring 79 goals and collecting ten trophies along the way.

His relentless work rate and important goals made him a popular figure among supporters, and the warmth of Sunday's reception demonstrated that bond remains intact despite his departure.

articles.title: Liverpool's transfer strategy facing biggest change in years
articles.summary: Liverpool are in a period of transition as a club, and more big changes are coming.  Since last season ended, Arne Slot, Michael Edwards and Richard Hughes h...
articles.body:
Liverpool are in a period of transition as a club, and more big changes are coming.

Since last season ended, Arne Slot, Michael Edwards and Richard Hughes have all moved on from Anfield.

As well as this backroom turnover, 1892 Holdings recently agreed a deal to buy close to 40% of the club from current owners Fenway Sports Group.

The Reds' Boston-based owners still have a controlling interest in the club, and were responsible for the appointment of Andoni Iraola , but big changes could be coming in Merseyside.

Now, as Liverpool look to appoint a new sporting director, their whole recruitment strategy could face a shakeup.

Liverpool to change recruitment approach

For many years now Liverpool have entrusted the duty of leading the recruitment team to a director of football, something that has been generally very successful at Anfield.

Figures like Edwards, Julian Ward, Jorg Schmadtke and Hughes have held the role at Liverpool, but the club might now be moving away from their traditional approach.

According to a report from Sky Sports , the club are seriously considering re-appointing Julian Ward as sporting director, but are also looking at hiring someone to work as co-sporting director with Brentford 's Lee Dykes one of the leading candidates.

The second appointment could see someone, potentially Dykes, become the technical director at Anfield a role that doesn't currently exist.

It appears that the Reds, potentially under advice from Amit Bhatia, are exploring a more collaborative approach to leading recruitment.

Bhatia is the leader of the 1892 Holdings group, and the input from Liverpool's new minority owners could be what has encouraged the club to try a new approach.

Ward currently holds a role as FSG's global technical director, but is very familiar with Liverpool's recruitment team having overseen the arrival of multiple current first-team players during his previous tenure as sporting director.

It remains to be seen which direction Liverpool will head in, but there could be big changes on the horizon behind the scenes in Merseyside.

articles.title: Mike Macdonald recounts "Cold War" with Sean Payton over cheating suspicions during the 2024 season
articles.summary: The Week 6 game between the Broncos and Seahawks has gained a new subplot.
articles.body:
The Week 6 game between the Broncos and Seahawks has gained a new subplot.

During an appearance on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald recounted a story involving Broncos head coach Sean Payton from his first season in Seattle. The Seahawks played the Broncos in Week 1 that year and Macdonald said that the team's staff collected fan videos posted to social media from Broncos practices as part of their preparation because they were "public knowledge."

The Seahawks won 26-20 and Macdonald said Payton "got wind of" how they used the videos in the middle of the season. Payton called Seahawks General Manager John Schneider and, per Macdonald, "lost it."

"He basically threatened to come out publicly and do a whole Patriot Spygate type of thing," Macdonald said. "I'm sitting there like, 'Oh my god. We didn't cheat.' They thought it was a Michigan thing where we had a plant and the whole thing. So we had to counter with him and say, 'If you come out with this, we're going to sue you because it's not true.'"

Macdonald said that Payton eventually dropped the issue, but that it felt like the two teams were involved in something more geopolitical than football until that happened.

"It was like the Cold War," Macdonald said. "He's like, 'I'm going to hit the button. I'm going to hit the button.' 'Well, we're going to hit the button.' None of us hit the button."

Macdonald said he and Payton subsequently crossed paths at the Scouting Combine, but the issue didn't come up. Payton will likely be asked about his version of events at some point before the Week 6 meeting between the teams.

articles.title: Saints move on from promising running back with injury settlement
articles.summary: This is disappointing. Rather than wait for him to heal up from a thigh injury, the New Orleans Saints cut Audric Estime with an injury settlement.
articles.body:
Good luck on your next opportunity, Audric Estime . ESPN's Katherine Terrell reported Tuesday that the New Orleans Saints waived the running back from injured reserve with an injury settlement, giving Estime the opportunity to play for another team once he's finished recovering from a thigh injury.

It's disappointing to see him move on after Estime ran hard throughout the summer, appearing to move ahead of guys like Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson on the depth chart. But he got hurt at the wrong time and other options have emerged with Alvin Kamara getting healthy and Donaldson making a role for himself as a position-flexible blocker and short-yardage specialist. Miller was a healthy scratch in Week 2's upset win over the Baltimore Ravens . With Zamir White on the practice squad and Travis Etienne Jr. still on top of the depth chart (in theory; Alvin Kamara got more touches against the Ravens), the team must have felt comfortable letting Estime walk away.

How do injury settlements work? Teams will make players an offer to match the salary they would have missed while on injured reserve, sometimes going to arbitration after the player seeks a second opinion on their recovery time. By essentially buying out the contract, teams can lighten the workload on their medical staff while giving the player a chance to suit up for another team once healthy. Estime will continue his rehab on his own but gets some money up front. It's possible he could re-sign with the Saints after getting the medical green light, but NFL rules require players to wait an extra three weeks after the settlement terms expire before they can go back to the same team. That encourages players to seek work elsewhere and prevents teams from cheating the injured reserve rules. So if Estime's settlement pays him for six weeks of recovery, he could re-sign with the Saints until nine weeks have passed.

articles.title: GTA 6 Could Turn November Into a Disaster for Sports Leagues, Predicts NBA Star
articles.summary: An NBA star has predicted that the release of the highly anticipated GTA 6 might lead to a drop in performance across the leagues The post GTA 6 Could Turn N...
articles.body:
An NBA star has predicted that the release of the highly anticipated GTA 6 might lead to a drop in performance across the leagues. The star also predicts that coaching and scouting will suffer as the next installment in the Grand Theft Auto series returns after a 13-year wait.

Steven Adams revealed on media day that he believes the release of GTA will impact league-wide performance in November. However, he is also sure that such dips in quality will be temporary yet inevitable.

Why Steven Adams thinks GTA 6 will distract more than just players

Steven Adams thinks that the focus on games would take a hit as GTA 6 releases. GTA 5 came out in 2013, and there hasn't been a game in the mainline franchise since. There is therefore no data yet to support the prediction. Nonetheless, Adams is sure that the game's launch will affect players, coaches, and scouts alike in November.

He stated, "I will say, you guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping. So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is gonna go down. It should come back up though, most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are gonna be horrendous, mate."

In sports, off-field events are rarely considered when evaluating player performance. Aside from personal and major events, it is usually expected that nothing will affect a player's performance beyond his mindset during the game. However, GTA 6's release could, as Adams predicts, lead to a subtle loss of focus. However, he is also confident that any dip in player performance will be reversed just as quickly in December.

articles.title: Milan Momcilovic is back to practice and looking good for Kentucky Basketball
articles.summary: The sharpshooter also celebrated his birthday today.
articles.body:
The BBN let out a collective gasp when news broke that Kentucky Basketball star Milan Momcilovic suffered an injury to a finger on his shooting hand. Even though it's the offseason and the injury was initially reported as simply being "severely jammed," just hearing about any problem with Momcilovic's shooting hand was a tough pill to swallow.

However, there's great news to report as the new season draws closer.

On Tuesday, the Wildcats took the floor for their first official practice of the 2026-27 college basketball season, and Momcilovic was active getting shots up.

The UK media team didn't waste a golden opportunity to show fans that everything seems to be right on track for Mark Pope's "sniper," and barring any setbacks, this shouldn't affect Momcilovic's ability to score the rock this winter.

I actually had the chance to watch Momcilovic get shots up last week when Kentucky hosted Media Madness inside the Joe Craft Center. He looked fine to me, and as you can see from the video, there appear to be nothing but positive developments in healing his jammed finger.

Again, there were no worries or scuttlebutt about this being anything other than minor from the beginning, but it was still reassuring to see the Iowa State transfer letting the ball fly while seemingly pain-free.

Of course, there is still a visible splint that's being worn, but you can only assume that will stay in place as a precautionary measure for as long as needed. UK will open the season in 42 days on Nov. 3rd when they take on Manhattan inside Rupp Arena.

The Cats will obviously lean heavily on Momcilovic to provide a huge chunk of their offense throughout a long season. But today, let the young man enjoy his special day as he celebrates his 22nd birthday.

articles.title: Jason Bilinski returns as Millville wrestling's head coach
articles.summary: Jason Bilinski returns as Millville High School wrestling head coach while Scott Stay moves to assistant.
articles.body:
The Millville High School wrestling program is undergoing a switch at the top again.

Jason Bilinski is back as the mat boss while former head coach Scott Stay is expected to remain with the Thunderbolts as an assistant coach. Bilinski was approved by the school board on Monday night.

Bilinski returns to the top position he held for eight seasons before he was moved into an assistant role last winter. He led the Thunderbolts to an 18-4 mark and a Cape-Atlantic League National Division title in the 2024-25 season.

"I always wanted to take it back over after I dealt with some personal matters last year," Bilinski said. "I couldn't not be around it, so I took on a lesser role. In any case, with Scott, it's like we have two head coaches anyway. It's just a title, really."

Bilinski said the program's biggest challenge is getting more athletes out for the team. After experiencing an increase in participation numbers in previous years, the Thunderbolts' roster was a little smaller last winter.

Millville athletic director Jason Kessler believes Bilinski's ability to develop multi-sport athletes into successful wrestlers will be key to the program.

"Jason is very passionate about the success of this program," Kessler said. "He's very good at getting multi-sport athletes to go out for wrestling and turn their skills developed in other sports into success on the mat."

After a standout wrestling career at Delsea where he won two Region 8 titles and later was a two-time All-American at Dana College in Nebraska, Bilinski had several coaching stints, including Gloucester County College (now Rowan College of South Jersey-Gloucester) before landing at Millville.

Stay was Millville's head coach for 14 years from 2003-2017 before taking over the program again last winter and guiding the Thunderbolts to a 6-13 record.

Tom McGurk is a regional sports editor for the Courier-Post, The Daily Journal and Burlington County Times, covering South Jersey sports for over 40 years. articles.title: Caleb Banks is stepping into his first round draft stock
articles.summary: Caleb Banks made plays on Sunday and the Vikings took notice of it.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings ' defense came out to play and kept the Bears ' offense from getting going. The weather made things messy, but the Vikings did just enough to let Will Reichard 's leg do the work.

They made plays at critical moments and contained the Bears ' offense overall. While Caleb Williams had a tough time, D'Andre Swift and their run game didn't do much better. One reason they struggled was that rookie and top pick by the Vikings in April, Caleb Banks, played more snaps and made them count in Week 2.

Speaking to the media after the game , head coach Kevin O'Connell made sure to offer his praise to Banks.

"The physical talent's clearly there, and the upside is there for us all to see, and we're just going to keep pushing him. I think (Defensive Running Game Coordinator Ryan) Nielsen doing a great job with him, but we've got to keep it going and see where his ascension can get to."

So far, both Banks and Domonique Orange have played exceptionally well up front. Both seem like they are poised for long tenures with the team and they are enjoying the youth infusion on defense.

articles.title: 3 things the Eagles can build on after Week 2 win over Titans
articles.summary: The Eagles found several encouraging developments against the Titans that they can build on entering Monday night against Chicago
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles didn't leave Nashville after a perfect performance , but they did leave with what every team wants heading into the next week. They found evidence of what can work. Some of those developments came from players stepping into expanded roles, while others involved decisions that could give Nick Sirianni and his staff more flexibility moving forward.

They allowed a 20-17 fourth-quarter lead to disappear, struggled to run the football consistently, and needed a last-minute touchdown drive to escape with a 24-20 victory . Nick Sirianni and his coaching staff have plenty to clean up before Monday night's matchup with the Chicago Bears .

However, there's another way to look at what happened against the Tennessee Titans . Philadelphia wasn't simply lucky enough to stumble into another win. The Eagles got meaningful contributions from players who weren't necessarily expected to carry the offense.

They showed they could control the game for long stretches. Those are the kinds of developments that can become useful over a season. Injuries forced some of them. Others came from players taking advantage of opportunities. Either way, Philadelphia now has more information about what works, and several successes from the Titans game are worth carrying into Week 3.

Give Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley more carries

Here's what no one is mentioning enough: Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley ran behind the same offensive line as Saquon Barkley , yet both youngsters looked comfortable when they got opportunities.

They aren't Saquon Barkley, and nobody should pretend otherwise, but that doesn't mean Philadelphia has to view the running back position as an all-or-nothing proposition. Bigsby and Shipley combined for 57 rushing yards on 20 carries, and Bigsby scored Philadelphia's first touchdown. That was enough to make a committee approach intriguing, especially if the Eagles can use the different skill sets of all their backs to keep defenses guessing.

Philadelphia shouldn't need a Saquon Barkley injury to revisit that idea.

Eagles played without committing penalties.

Philadelphia cleaned up its penalty problem again, committing four penalties for 35 yards compared with five for 40 yards in the opener. That's not exactly a headline-worthy improvement, but that's the point.

The Eagles are finding ways to operate with fewer self-inflicted setbacks, and that should matter more as the competition gets tougher. Clean football gives a talented roster a better chance to let its talent decide games.

Philadelphia held the football for 36:25 against Tennessee, winning the time-of-possession battle and limiting the Titans' opportunities to stay on the field. That could become even more valuable against Chicago and Ben Johnson's offense.

Every minute the Eagles control the football is a minute Johnson's offense isn't on the field. Philadelphia doesn't have to dominate possession to win. Still, another ball-control performance that keeps Chicago's offense standing on the sideline for long stretches would go a long way toward creating the kind of game the Eagles want to play.

articles.title: Titans’ kickoff strategy raising red flags after Eagles loss
articles.summary: The Titans’ kickoff strategy is raising red flags after a costly touchback helped give the Eagles favorable field position late in Week 2.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans ' special teams strategy is drawing attention after a costly kickoff decision in their Week 2 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles .

With 1:56 remaining and Philadelphia out of timeouts, the Titans chose to kick the ball through the end zone for a touchback. That decision gave the Eagles possession at their own 35-yard line and proved valuable as Philadelphia marched down the field and scored the game-winning touchdown with just nine seconds remaining.

The Titans ultimately lost 24-20, and the decision has raised questions about Tennessee's approach to kickoffs, especially after opening the season with a penalty on their opening kickoff in Week 1 against the New York Jets .

Through the first two weeks of the 2026 season, the Titans have kicked the ball into the end zone on three of six non-onside kickoffs, according to Ryan Paganetti. That number is 50%, which leads the NFL by a wide margin, with no other team above 33.3% this season.

According to the data Ryan Paganetti shared in the post, kicks landing between the one- and five-yard lines produce an average starting field position at the 29.5-yard line and take six seconds off the clock.

That difference can matter most late in games, as the Titans experienced. Their Week 2 loss reminds us that special teams decisions may not look significant in the moment, but they matter when the final seconds arrive. For a team trying to become winners, those small details could matter more than you think.

articles.title: Yankees lose Aaron Judge before their worst series of the year
articles.summary: The Yankees got the Aaron Judge news at a brutal time. He was placed on the 10-day injured list retroactive […]
articles.body:
The Yankees got the Aaron Judge news at a brutal time. He was placed on the 10-day injured list retroactive to Sept. 17 with a right calf strain, and now Tampa Bay is in town for a doubleheader that starts the biggest stretch on the schedule.

Judge has played only 66 games, yet he still owns an .871 OPS and 18 homers. Take Aaron Judge out of the middle of this lineup for any length of time and the order stops looking like a problem for pitchers.

Carlos Rodon gets the ball in Game 1 on Tuesday afternoon, Max Fried follows at night, and the Yankees need both games. They are not walking into a soft landing after an injury. They are walking straight into the Rays .

The Yankees have no room for a quiet series

This is the sort of series where Judge would normally be the whole point of the conversation. He changes how opponents pitch the hitters around him, whether he is getting the big hit or simply forcing a bullpen decision earlier than planned.

The Yankees have recalled Max Schuemann after the Judge move, and he can help fill an active roster spot. No one is pretending he fills Judge's spot in the lineup. There is no clean substitute for a hitter who can change a score with one plate appearance.

That puts more pressure on the regulars to make the game shorter. Get traffic on base. Cash in the innings that start with a leadoff man aboard. Do not wait around for a three-run shot that may not be coming.

Tampa Bay is the wrong opponent for the Yankees to be shorthanded

The Yankees have enough pitching lined up to make this a real fight. Rodon and Fried are exactly the arms they would want for a doubleheader with the division on the line. The lineup is the part that feels exposed.

Judge's calf has to come first. Nobody should ask him to rush back for a September series. But the Yankees also cannot treat this like a normal injury absence and expect the standings to wait for them. Every at-bat without him gets heavier over the next few days.

articles.title: Brewers news: Pat Murphy drops 'beautiful' admission on Jacob Misiorowski's historic season
articles.summary: With Milwaukee Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski having a legitimate historic season for the team, he looks to continue to help the team into the postseason. As...
articles.body:
With Milwaukee Brewers star Jacob Misiorowski having a legitimate historic season for the team, he looks to continue to help the team into the postseason. As the Brewers prepare for the 2026 MLB Playoffs , manager Pat Murphy would reflect on Misiorowski's performance this past season compared to 2025.

Speaking on "The Pat McAfee Show," Murphy was asked about his thoughts on seeing Misiorowski evolve from last season to the current time, emphasizing how much of a "beautiful story" it is. Murphy would express that the biggest difference is that he's grown as a teammate in Milwaukee.

"He's a beautiful kid, first and foremost, if you watch his operation off the field, it's him, his fiancée, his mom and dad, and it's beautiful," Murphy said. "Like they're just this little unit. He has no idea he's the Miz. It's kind of Forrest Gump-like. Like he's just being who he's being. He can't change. He takes it all in stride. The biggest difference is this year he's a great teammate. He's not looking to fit in. Last year he didn't kind of know how he fit."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Pat Murphy continues on Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski

Misiorowski appears to be a lock for the NL Cy Young Award as he's recorded an MLB-leading 1.86 ERA, 0.80 WHIP, and 186 strikeouts, to go along with a 15-5 record. Murphy highlighted how Misiorowski's delivery "is so much more consistent."

"And then seeing him respond the way he did at the end of last year, and then going in the offseason and training the way he trained and got himself so much stronger, so therefore his delivery is so much more consistent," Murphy said. "He still's got no idea what he's doing, but it's just fun, the maturation. You know, he's taking that next step. But like I said, there's many more steps to take. He is kind of a freak a little bit in that his extension is so good, coupled with his velo, and he's a great teammate, a great person. It's kind of fun."

It remains to be seen how Misiorowski and the Brewers close out the 2026 season.

articles.title: Giants’ worst Jaxson Dart fear is now on the table
articles.summary: The Giants went from relief to real concern in less than a day. Further testing on Jaxson Dart’s left knee […]
articles.body:
The Giants went from relief to real concern in less than a day. Further testing on Jaxson Dart 's left knee found an injury more serious than the team first believed, and he may be facing season-ending surgery.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the team and Dart are now confronting that possibility. The Giants have not announced a final diagnosis or a surgery decision, but the initial hope that this was a manageable sprained MCL is gone.

The injury happened on the opening drive of Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Rams. Dart did not return, and Jameis Winston handled the rest of the game. What looked like a short-week quarterback question has turned into a much larger problem for the season.

The Giants are staring at a season-changing decision

There is still a lot the Giants have not said publicly. Nobody should invent a recovery timetable, diagnose the injury from a clip, or treat surgery as official before the club does.

The report itself is enough to change the conversation. Dart is expected to miss an extended period, and the season is now part of that discussion. That means the Giants have to consider a plan without the quarterback they built the offense around.

I would not bury the season on Sept. 22. I also would not frame this as a one-week injury and move on. Dart has been the player who made this offense feel different, and losing him for any serious stretch changes what every game looks like.

The Giants have to adjust to life without Dart for now

The immediate football answer points to Winston, but the issue goes past naming a starter for Tennessee . The Giants need to decide how much of the offense stays intact, how much they can ask from their backup, and whether they need another quarterback in the building.

Dart had just started the season with a 23-of-29, three-touchdown performance against Dallas . The Giants had a reason to believe they could take a real step forward. The latest injury update has put all of that on hold.

articles.title: Youth Hockey Player Suspended After Aggressively Slashing Opponent with Stick
articles.summary: The game between two rival teams in Massachusetts became violent on Saturday, Sept. 19
articles.body:
A youth hockey game got violent in Massachusetts over the weekend

During a game, a player viciously slashed an opponent with his stick

The young attacker was ejected and is facing a lengthy suspension

A youth hockey player has been suspended after viciously stick-slashing an opponent during a game over the weekend.

The hit — which has gone viral — happened during a game between mostly 11-year-old boys on the South Shore Kings and Bay State Breakers in Foxboro, Mass., on Saturday, Sept 19.

In video shared by 7News (Warning: Explicit language), the Bay State player surprised the Kings skater from behind and hit him in the face with his stick. Both fell to the ice, with the attacker's stick breaking in half.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

After a referee quickly skated between the two boys, the victim was able to skate off the ice on his own, while the Bay State player was immediately ejected from the game.

Onlookers said the two players were involved in a tussle at mid-ice before the attack.

According to the father of the victim, the boy is okay after the incident.

Meanwhile, the Breakers player faces a lengthy suspension from the ice.

"The Breakers player has been suspended indefinitely from practices and games," a Bay State Breakers representative told 7NEWS.

Massachusetts Hockey, which oversees the teams, told 7NEWS that they are "aware of the incident and it is being handled in accordance with Massachusetts Hockey and USA Hockey's discipline processes."

articles.title: Jaxson Dart injury: Giants must not let Jameis Winston sabotage season
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart suffered a gruesome knee injury in the New York Giants’ 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams during Monday Night Football. Initial reports suggested...
articles.body:
Jaxson Dart suffered a gruesome knee injury in the New York Giants ' 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams during Monday Night Football. Initial reports suggested that the quarterback may have avoided a significant injury. Head coach John Harbaugh even said that a " devastating outcome" was avoided with Dart's knee.

However, further testing has told a different story. Now it is believed that Dart's injury is significant and will hold him out for a long period of time, with his season as a whole coming to a close being a realistic possibility. Dart was replaced in Week 2 by Jameis Winston , who is the only other quarterback on the active 53-man roster.

The fan-favorite, who was signed to a two-year contract extension less than a month ago, has had an up-and-down career. He really struggled under center against the Rams, though, and the Giants need to ensure the former Heisman winner doesn't tank their season.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Jameis Winston is a high-risk, high-reward player

Winston was the number one pick back in 2015. The Florida State product oftentimes put up huge numbers with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of his willingness to attempt big plays. However, Winston's risk-taking nature has also led to costly mistakes and high interception numbers. For example, in 2019 Winston led the league with 5,109 yards but also had a league-leading 30 interceptions.

The story was the same during his tenures with the New Orleans Saints and Cleveland Browns . Regardless, the Giants extended the quarterback because he is someone who can go out and win his team a game, which is a rarity for backup signal callers. The team knew that the backup QB position was important, too, because Dart has regularly put his body at risk to injury throughout his young career.

While this most recent injury wasn't Dart's fault, the Giants were well aware that Winston could see playing time at some point this year. Winston was just 11 for 27 for 111 yards when thrust into action in Week 2. He had no touchdowns and threw an interception, too. Of course, coming into a game in relief is never easy, but Winston got paid big bucks for a backup quarterback so he'd be ready to go when called upon.

The Giants are 1-1, but they have a core that is ready to compete for the postseason right now. The team is loaded with weapons, which include a running back trio of Cam Skattebo , Najee Harris , and Devin Singletary , as well as pass catchers like Isaiah Likely , Malachi Fields , and Malik Nabers .

The Giants blamed their struggles last season on injuries, but they can't use that excuse two years in a row. Winston needs to perform, and that means cutting down on the game-altering mistakes that have plagued him throughout his career. If the former number one pick can't figure things out, especially after receiving QB1 reps in practice, the Giants might have to look at alternatives at the quarterback position, assuming that Dart will be out for the year.

articles.title: Changes made to route for 2026 TCS New York City Marathon
articles.summary: For the first time in 15 years, the iconic five-borough course of the TCS New York City Marathon is changing -- but only slightly.
articles.body:
For the first time in 15 years, the iconic five-borough course of the TCS New York City Marathon is changing -- but only slightly.

The affected portion involves a roughly mile-long stretch in the Bronx.

The old course had previously looped around a block that included a supermarket, which effectively cut it off from people in the neighborhood during the race.

The new route loops around a different block, completely avoiding the grocery store.

Starting this year, after crossing the Willis Avenue Bridge, runners will:

Turn right on Alexander Avenue and continuing straight on Alexander Avenue-instead of making a left on E 138th Street

Turn right onto E 138th Street to continue across the Madison Avenue Bridge

To learn more about the 2026 TCS New York City Marathon, click here .

ABC 7 / WABC-TV and ESPN2 have been home to the award-winning TCS New York City Marathon broadcast since 2013.

articles.title: Ravens Reacts Survey: biggest concern heading into Week 2
articles.summary: Take this week’s Ravens Reacts survey to share your biggest concerns after Baltimore’s Week 2 loss to the Saints!
articles.body:
Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country.

After a complete victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 1, the Baltimore Ravens looked disarrayed in all phases of their Week 2 to the New Orleans Saints .

It's no surprise that a new head coach and a first-time offensive play-caller are facing some early-season bumps. What matter is their response. Past Ravens squads faced similar issues and stayed stuck in neutral for some, if not all of the season.

Sunday's defeat in Baltimore exposed a number of flaws. In this week's Ravens Reacts survey, we want to know which one is the biggest concern for the Ravens moving forward. Here's the case for each:

OL pass protection: The Ravens' new-look offensive line has yet to find their footing in front of Lamar Jackson , who has been one of the league's most-blitzed and -pressured quarterbacks through two weeks. Baltimore also owns the NFL's worst team pass-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus . This has been the downfall of the offense for multiple years; Doyle and offensive line coach Dwayne Ledford to get the unit settled in as quickly as possible.

3rd down defense: Minter's defense held the Colts to a 4-for-11 mark on third and fourth downs in Week 1, but the Saints went 10-for-16 on Sunday. Part of the issue came on first and second down, when quick completions by Tyler Shough would keep New Orleans ahead of the sticks. Baltimore had numerous opportunities to stop the bleeding and get off the field in the second half, but they could not dig their heels in for a stop. After Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green wiped out a third-quarter drive with a pair of sacks, the pass rush did not get home for the rest of the game. That is not quite "being the best when the best is needed."

Special teams: Anthony Levine 's units took care of business in Week 1 with a number of chunk returns, solid coverage, and perfect days from kicker Tyler Loop and punter Ryan Eckley. But in Week 2, Loop had a 49-yard field goal blocked, Eckley averaged just 41.3 yards per punt with zero inside the 20-yard line, and the Ravens lost the field position battle on returns and coverage. Beatdown's Zach Canter noted a potential nine-point swing as a result of special teams miscues that should simply not happen with this roster's talent and coaching.

Injuries: The Ravens' depth is already being tested by early-season injuries. Left tackle Ronnie Stanley played through his toe injury for more than half of Sunday's game, but he eventually gave way to backup Carson Vinson . The 2025 fifth-round pick had his hands full with Chase Young , who was instrumental in helping the Saints defense close out the game. Wide receiver Zay Flowers missed the entire matchup with a hamstring injury; there were certainly times in the second half he would have made a difference.

Now, it's your turn! Answer this week's survey below or in The Feed and share your additional thoughts in the comments section!

Are the Ravens headed in the right direction?

articles.title: 4 issues the Ravens must correct before facing Cowboys in Brazil
articles.summary: The Ravens don't need a dramatic overhaul after one loss, but several issues from the Saints game can't follow them to Brazil.
articles.body:
Though it may seem like the sky is falling, it isn't. The Baltimore Ravens are 1-1, not 0-2. There is no reason for panic after one disappointing Sunday afternoon.

At the same time, several lessons can be taken from their Week 2 loss to the New Orleans Saints . The frustrating part for Baltimore is that many of the mistakes were self-inflicted.

The Ravens led 17-9 entering the fourth quarter. They had opportunities to extend the lead. They had opportunities to put the game away. Instead, New Orleans left Baltimore with a 24-17 victory . With a matchup against the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil ahead, here are four issues the Ravens must correct before Week 3.

Tyler Loop can't be a roller-coaster ride.

No, Tyler Loop hasn't been awful. Yes, there is a reasonable argument that his missed field goal against New Orleans would have been good if it hadn't been tipped at the line of scrimmage. Sometimes special teams plays don't go your way.

Still, a miss is a miss, and questions remain. The simplest way to measure confidence in a kicker is to ask one question: If the Ravens need a field goal to win in the final seconds against Dallas, how comfortable are you with Loop jogging onto the field?

The answer probably differs depending on who you ask, but Baltimore needs that answer to become unanimous sooner rather than later. The Ravens have been spoiled by elite kicking for years. Whether fair or unfair, every kick will be evaluated through that lens.

Ravens can't travel into Cowboys territory and come away with no points

This might have been Baltimore's most frustrating issue against New Orleans. The Ravens had multiple opportunities to add points and failed to capitalize. On their final possession, the Ravens reached the Saints ' 37-yard line before Lamar Jackson 's deep pass was intercepted by Julian Blackmon with 13 seconds remaining.

Earlier, Baltimore forced a three-and-out while holding a 17-9 lead. Sacks by Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green led to a bad punt, one that gave the Ravens the ball at the New Orleans 49-yard line late in the third quarter.

It felt like a perfect opportunity to create separation. Instead, a pre-snap penalty helped derail the drive. Baltimore went backward, and the possession ended with a punt.

Three drives that either started in or crossed into Saints territory produced zero points. Dallas has allowed opponents to move the football through two weeks. The Ravens will likely have scoring opportunities in Brazil. They cannot leave points on the field.

Ravens can't extend drives or give Cowboys extra opportunities

The penalty count wasn't outrageous against New Orleans. The timing, however, was devastating. After Chris Olave 's touchdown cut Baltimore's lead to two points, the Ravens appeared to stop the Saints on a two-point conversion attempt.

Then came a penalty that moved the ball closer to the goal line. New Orleans attempted the two-point conversion again and scored on the second opportunity. Travis Etienne Jr. tied the game at 17.

Those are the types of mistakes that swing momentum and change outcomes. Dallas has too many offensive weapons to be gifted additional chances. If Baltimore gets the Cowboys off the field, it has to stay that way.

Derrick Henry can't be given 16 carries in a close game.

Sixteen carries for 68 yards is a respectable afternoon for most running backs. Derrick Henry is not most running backs. Baltimore handed him the ball 16 times in a game that remained competitive throughout. Even more surprising was the decision to have him watch a critical short-yardage situation from the sideline. The Ravens ran the football only 22 times as a team.

Against an explosive Cowboys offense, ball control may become one of Baltimore's greatest weapons. Sustaining drives keeps Lamar Jackson on the field and limits opportunities for Dak Prescott and Dallas' playmakers. That starts with Henry.

Nobody is asking Baltimore to force-feed the future Hall of Famer. At the same time, it is hard to imagine many Ravens fans complaining if Henry gets 20 or more carries in Brazil. When one of the NFL's most physical runners is on your roster, close games should generally include a healthy dose of No. 22.

The Ravens don't need to reinvent themselves after one loss. They do, however, need to clean up the mistakes that helped turn a winnable game into a frustrating defeat. If they can accomplish that, Week 2 may ultimately serve as a valuable lesson rather than the beginning of a troubling trend.

articles.title: Kentucky's Kenny Darby among top week three freshman per PFF
articles.summary: Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby overcame an early drop to lead the Wildcats to victory, proving his mental toughness.
articles.body:
The sun hung high and merciless over the Brazos Valley on Saturday, the way it does in Texas in September, a white-hot midday glare with no shade to be found, and under it stood a stadium built for giants. A hundred thousand voices in maroon. A band that marches like an army. A defense ranked among the nation's best, waiting in the heat for a team from the bluegrass that nobody had asked to come.

And into that, carrying nothing but a number on his jersey and a mistake on his conscience, walked an 18-year-old Kentucky Wildcats receiver named Kenny Darby .

Legends do not always begin with a triumph. Sometimes they begin with the ball on the ground.

When the week's numbers came in, Pro Football Focus graded Darby at 78.6, sixth-best among all true freshmen in the country. And that grade includes a play he'd like to have back. The graders saw the whole body of work, the good and the bad, and still had him in the top 10. That tells you the good was really good.

Let's talk about what really happened, because what happened in the first quarter matters more than people think.

Darby gets behind the coverage. Kenny Minchey puts it right on him. That's a touchdown. That's a play you're supposed to make, and he didn't make it. Now, the drive keeps going, you get down there close, and then you get a penalty, you take two sacks, you miss the kick. So you've got a seven-point swing that turns into a zero. In this league, against a top-10 team on the road, those are the kinds of things that get you beat.

But here's what I look for when I evaluate a young player. It's not whether you make a mistake. Everybody makes mistakes. Freshmen make a lot of them. It's what you do on the next play. Can you let it go? Can you stay focused on what's in front of you instead of what's behind you? Because the guys who can't do that, they drop one and then they drop two, and they're thinking about the last play while the next one's going on.

Darby let it go. His quarterback told him the ball was coming back to him. His head coach, Will Stein , told him he was fine. And then they proved they meant it.

First drive of the second half. Same kind of look. Minchey goes back to him, and this time he catches it, makes a guy miss, and it's 42 yards and a touchdown. Kentucky's first lead of the game. Then the next drive, they're backed up at their own 17, it's looking like three-and-out, and who do they throw it to? Darby again, for 22 yards and a first down. That drive ends in a touchdown. Now you're up 21-7, and you won 31-21.

Two catches, 64 yards. Some people are going to look at that and say it's not much. I'd say look at when those catches came. One gave you the lead. One kept a scoring drive alive when you were about to hand the ball back. That's winning football. That's affecting the game.

Now I'll say this, because it's important. One game doesn't make a player. He's got 10 catches, 183 yards, two touchdowns through three games, and he's Kentucky's leading receiver, and that's a nice start. But the SEC is going to see this film.

Defensive coordinators are going to know who he is now. He's going to get more attention, tighter coverage, maybe a safety over the top. The challenge for him is to keep improving, keep doing the little things right, and not get caught up in what everybody's saying about him.

Because what people say about you after a big game, that can be just as dangerous as a dropped ball. Maybe more.

Kentucky found this kid on the last day of the early signing period, flipped him away from LSU , and right now that looks like one of the better decisions anybody in that building has made. But the story isn't the catch. The story is the drop, and the fact that it didn't beat him.

The sun will rise again over Lexington this week as the Cats prep for South Alabama at Kroger Field, and somewhere in it a young receiver will be back at practice, catching balls from the JUGS machine until his hands ache. That's how the next one gets caught.
authors: Lee Ann Herring Olvedo, UK Wildcats Wire
